abstract_ko: This study explores how four female Mandarin Chinese-speaking L2 learners at a U.S. university engage with machine translation (MT) in English writing and develop strategies to navigate its affordances and limitations. The participants completed both MT-assisted and non-MT-assisted writing tasks. Using Activity Theory as a framework, the study qualitatively examines how MT functions as a mediating artifact, shaping students’ writing processes through technological affordances, academic expectations, and individual agency. The findings reveal that while most students used MT for grammar and lexical choice, one student critically assessed its limitations and actively sought alternative strategies, such as peer feedback and writing center support. The findings underscore the varied and strategic ways L2 learners engage with MT and highlight how contradictions in its use can foster meaningful adaptation. This study contributes to a deeper understanding of digital mediation in L2 writing and offers pedagogical implications for integrating MT to support learner autonomy and metalinguistic awareness.

abstract_ko: This study explores how machine-learning technique can enhance text selection in primary English education by clustering textbook dialogues according to their communicative functions and by classifying picture-book texts within the same framework. 484 dialogue texts from five publishers’ Grade 3~6 textbooks were vectorized and clustered with an unsupervised algorithm. 13 clusters aligned perfectly with a single communcative functions, while 32 clusters showed high concordance when second-most frequent function was also considered. The validated cluster labels served as training data in a logistic-regression classifier that assigned seven English picture books to curriculum-specified communicative functions. Four picture books were classified with high probability for a single function, confirming that models trained on textbook dialogues can credibly map out-of-textbook reading materials onto the curriculum. Educationally, the approach furnishes an objective tool for teachers to identify picture-book texts that reinforce the communicative goals of a given unit. More broadly, it demonstrates that quantitative text analytics can reveal latent connections between mandated textbooks and external resources, offering a scalable pathway toward more coherent and diversified input in primary English classrooms.

abstract_ko: This study explored how elementary English teachers conceptualized and implemented English–AI convergence classes. Four elementary school teachers participated, and data were collected through semi-structured interviews and reflective journals. The data were analyzed qualitatively using content analysis. Findings revealed that teachers held varying perceptions of English–AI convergence instruction: some viewed it as an aspect of interdisciplinary teaching, while others regarded it as a form of curriculum-level restructuring. Motivations for implementation included intrinsic interest and awareness of AI’s instructional potential. Teachers expressed significant concern about the lack of applicable instructional models, as well as ethical and technical challenges. In practice, they utilized diverse AI tools to tailor lessons to classroom contexts. Reported outcomes included enhanced personalized learning and increased student engagement. However, challenges such as students’ overreliance on AI, limited teacher preparedness, and inadequate infrastructure were also noted. Teachers emphasized the need for high-quality, context-sensitive professional development and proposed improvements in teacher education, school environments, educational platforms, and policy support. As AI technologies continue to advance in education, addressing teachers’ perceptions and building their competencies is essential for meaningful integration. This study offers practical insights and suggests directions for the sustainable implementation of English–AI convergence instruction in elementary education.

title_ko: Development and Application of AI Agents for Elementary English Writing Assessment: Focusing on a Comparison with ChatGPT
title_en: Development and Application of AI Agents for Elementary English Writing Assessment: Focusing on a Comparison with ChatGPT
kw_en: elementary English education; writing assessment; AI agents; automatic question generation; automated answer scoring
abstract_ko: This study developed and examined AIEEWA, a specialized AI agent system for elementary English writing assessment, by comparing its utility against the general-purpose model ChatGPT. AIEEWA comprises two agents: (a) an automatic question generation (AQG) agent that generates curriculum-aligned questions and rubrics and (b) an automated answer scoring (AAS) agent that scores answers and generates feedback. The system was developed by leveraging retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and self-evaluation mechanisms (Self-RAG, LLM-as-a-Judge) with GPT-4o. Its performance was evaluated using questions generated by the agent and writing samples collected from Korean students in the 5th and 6th grades. Results show that AIEEWA’s AQG agent generated questions with a higher average content validity than those generated by ChatGPT, although expert review remains indispensable. The AAS agent also demonstrated significantly higher intra-rater scoring reliability and feedback consistency than ChatGPT. In addition, although AIEEWA’s AAS agent achieved better inter-rater agreement with teacher consensus scores than ChatGPT, the agreement level was still moderate, underscoring the difficulty of fully replicating nuanced human judgment. These findings suggest that purpose-built AI agents such as AIEEWA can substantially enhance assessment efficiency and consistency compared with ChatGPT. At the current stage, however, they are better suited to assisting teachers rather than replacing them.

abstract_ko: This study aims to provide foundational data for developing perception-based training materials for pre-service teachers during the early implementation phase of AI Digital Textbooks (AIDT) in English education. A survey was conducted with 24 pre-service secondary English teachers to examine their perceptions of AI-based digital technology, AIDT evaluation criteria, and the educational effectiveness of AIDT. The results indicated that participants prioritized ethical use and social responsibility regarding AI technology. Among AIDT evaluation criteria, fairness, linguistic accuracy, and personalized learning support were rated as the most important. In terms of perceived educational benefits, AIDT was viewed as most effective in improving listening, viewing, and vocabulary skills, while writing and presenting skills received lower ratings. Correlation analysis revealed a significant relationship between participants‘ self-assessed English proficiency and their perceptions of AI application in teaching, particularly for speaking and viewing. However, no significant correlation was found between English proficiency and perceptions of AIDT evaluation criteria. Qualitative responses highlighted both optimism about personalized learning and concerns about learner health, attention, and classroom management. These findings suggest that pre-service teacher education should include differentiated, practice-based AIDT training, emphasize ethical and sustainable use, and offer tailored support based on teachers' language proficiency levels.

abstract_ko: This study explores the integration of ChatGPT, an AI language model, into an English for Tourism course designed for EFL learners. Amid the expanding use of Content-Based Instruction (CBI) and English for Specific Purposes (ESP) in language education, this research investigates how ChatGPT’s prompt-based feedback supports learners in overcoming challenges such as grammatical errors, appropriate stylistic usages, and audience-aware language use. Twenty university students engaged in a semester-long course involving three presentations on Korean tourist sites, where they composed, revised, and presented English tour guide texts with ChatGPT’s assistance. Results showed that ChatGPT not only aided in correcting errors but also enhanced learners’ ability to adjust vocabulary difficulty, differentiate between spoken and written styles, and produce contextually appropriate texts for diverse audiences. Survey data revealed increased learner confidence, motivation, and positive attitudes toward AI-assisted learning, although concerns about over-reliance and unnatural AI outputs were noted. The findings underscore ChatGPT’s potential as a cognitive scaffold in ESP education, emphasizing the need for explicit prompt training and critical engagement to maximize educational benefits.

abstract_ko: The purpose of this study is to compare English learners’ perceptions of evaluating and using machine translation (MT) output across different proficiency levels. A total of 60 participants took part in the study: 23 intermediate-level and 37 advancedlevel English learners. Participants were asked to assess the quality of translations produced by three different machine translators and to reflect on their use of such tools. Quantitative data were analyzed using frequency analysis and chi-square tests, while qualitative responses were examined through content analysis. The findings indicate that both groups were able to evaluate translation output appropriately in many cases, regardless of their proficiency. However, differences were also observed in the evaluation of specific results depending on the learners’ English levels. These findings highlight the importance of developing learners’ critical awareness when using MT tools and suggest the need for instructional support to foster more accurate and informed evaluation of machine-generated translations.

abstract_ko: 본 연구는 생성형 인공지능 기술의 발전이 문학 창작 및 문학교육에 미치는 영향을 비판적으로 검토하고, 그 결과에 근거하여 현대시 교육의 대응 방향을 제시하고자 하였다. 인공지능 기술의 발전으로 등장한 기술창작시대 담론은 문학과 문학교육의 패러다임 전환을 요청하고 있다. 생성형 인공지능 기술은 대규모 언어 모델에 기반한 복잡한 알고리즘으로 작동하면서도, 상당 부분 인간 주체의 개입을 필요로 한다는 점에서 창작 주체로서 일정한 한계를 지닌다. 본 연구는 인공지능 기술의 활용 정도에 따라, ‘도구로서의 인공지능’, ‘공동 주체로서의 인공지능’, ‘인공지능에 의한 창작’으로 범주화하여 생성형 인공지능 기술을 활용하여 창작된 현대시 작품 및 연구 성과를 분석하였다. 분석 결과 생성형 인공지능 기술을 문학 창작의 새로운 주체로 인정하려는 논의에는 여러 한계가 있으나, 한편으로 이러한 기술의 발전이 문학 작품을 교육 현장에서 다루는 방식에 일정 부분 변화를 요구하는 측면이 있음을 확인하였다. 이에 본 연구는 현대시 교육의 대응 방향으로 다음 세 가지를 제안하였다. 첫째, 창작의 과정에서 기획과 선별의 의미가 더욱 강조될 필요가 있다는 점, 둘째, 창작의 과정을 세분화하고 반복적 고쳐 쓰기를 활성화할 필요가 있다는 점, 셋째, 인공지능 기술을 활용한 창작에 적합한 이론을 문학교육의 장에 확장적으로 적용할 필요가 있다는 점이다. 본 연구는 기술창작시대 담론이 현실을 왜곡하거나, 해석 과잉의 양상으로 이루어지는 것을 경계하는 한편, 새로운 기술이 문학교육의 실천적 틀 안에서 의미 있게 적용될 수 있는 방향을 탐색하였다는 점에서 의미가 있다.

abstract_ko: This study investigates how ChatGPT was integrated into a 15-week problem-based learning (PBL) psycholinguistics course at a university in a metropolitan area in Korea. Seven undergraduate students participated in collaborative tasks and thematic explorations, investigating real-world cases related to language acquisition, cognitive processing, and cross-linguistic patterns, as well as other core topics. Thematic analysis of reflection journals, final reports, and instructor field notes revealed that ChatGPT enhanced students’ information access, conceptual understanding, critical thinking, and collaborative reasoning. Students developed prompting strategies, evaluated AI-generated responses, and connected theoretical concepts to real-world language experiences. ChatGPT also facilitated metacognitive regulation, enabling learners to monitor comprehension and adjust learning strategies accordingly. As a cognitive and strategic partner, ChatGPT fostered deeper engagement and learner autonomy. Notably, students used the tool to revise explanations, compare sources, generate questions, and visualize reasoning for presentations. During group collaboration, ChatGPT served as a discussion catalyst and helped students articulate and refine their perspectives. These findings suggest that generative AI, when thoughtfully integrated, can meaningfully support concept-oriented instruction in higher education contexts.

abstract_ko: This study explores the role of ChatGPT in enhancing vocabulary learning among high school students in Kazakhstan. Twenty-seven students participated in a two-week intervention that utilized ChatGPT within a mixed-methods framework. Data were collected through vocabulary assessments administered before and after the intervention, learner surveys at both stages, ChatGPT interaction logs, and follow-up interviews. The tests results were analyzed using a paired t-test. The findings revealed that the students engaged with ChatGPT in strategic and diverse ways, such as adjusting prompt difficulty, requesting translations or definitions, and exploring creative tasks. Many also demonstrated autonomies by generating their own prompts beyond the provided set. A statistically significant improvement in vocabulary scores was observed after the intervention. Students reported highly positive perceptions of ChatGPT, citing its constant availability, adaptive feedback, and flexibility in meeting individual learning needs. Although some technical challenges, like unstable internet connections, were noted, these issues were external to the tool itself. Overall, the study suggests that ChatGPT can be as a flexible and responsive resource for supporting vocabulary development and fostering learner autonomy in EFL contexts. This study also discusses limitations and pedagogical implications.

abstract_ko: This study investigated how ChatGPT can enhance L2 email writing, specifically focusing on politeness. Twenty-nine Korean university students were asked to draft an email in class requesting a recommendation letter from an English-speaking professor. For the assignment, they submitted their initial drafts to ChatGPT to receive guided feedback. Subsequently, they revised their drafts based on the politeness features observed in the ChatGPT-generated model email. Four days later, the participants wrote the same email again in class without ChatGPT’s assistance. The three versions of the emails were analyzed for address forms, levels of directness in the requests, and external modifications. The results indicated that ChatGPT had a significant immediate impact on the use of politeness features in the emails; however, many of these improvements diminished in the delayed post-task, except for sustained gains in email closings. These findings suggest that while ChatGPT can lead to immediate enhancements in L2 email politeness, explicit instruction may be necessary for ensuring long-term retention of these features.

title_en: Preparing teachers for artificial intelligence integration: A systematic review

abstract_ko: With the rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), preparing teachers for its effective integration has become increasingly important. This study aims to examine how recent research addressed teacher preparation for the integration of AI in English education. It investigates literature between 2020 and 2025 on AI integration in English education, with a focus on teacher preparation for AI use. Using a systematic review methodology guided by Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses framework, 45 relevant studies were identified and analyzed. The findings reveal a growing interest in AI integration. However, significant gaps remain in teacher preparation. While many studies highlight improvements in teachers’ attitudes and perceived competence following AI-focused training, there is limited evidence of actual classroom application. The literature is dominated by perception-based research and relies heavily on self-reported data. Moreover, many qualitative studies lacked methodological transparency, limiting the reliability of their findings. These results suggest a pressing need for future research to adopt more rigorous and context-sensitive designs. Importantly, the study underscores the value of developing practical, classroom-oriented teacher training programs that go beyond raising awareness and address real instructional challenges in AI implementation.

abstract_ko: This study investigates the short- and long-term effects of two types of written corrective feedback (WCF)—direct feedback and reformulation—delivered via ChatGPT on EFL learners’ writing performance. Twenty-seven university students participated in a three-stage writing process: an initial draft, a first revision immediately after feedback, and a delayed second revision two weeks later without additional support. Writing was evaluated across five dimensions: Content, Organization, Vocabulary, Language Use, and Mechanics. Descriptive and inferential analyses revealed that both feedback types led to short-term improvements, particularly in Content, Vocabulary, and overall writing scores. Direct WCF was effective in generating broad improvements across most areas, excluding Language Use. Reformulation feedback, in contrast, led to stronger gains in Content and Organization and continued to yield significant improvements in the delayed revision, especially in Content and Vocabulary. However, neither feedback type produced significant gains in grammatical accuracy (Language Use), indicating the need for supplementary grammar instruction. These findings suggest that reformulation feedback via ChatGPT is particularly effective in enhancing idea development and lexical variety, while direct WCF provides general but less targeted improvements. The study highlights the pedagogical potential of AI-mediated feedback and underscores the importance of differentiated instructional strategies to address persistent language accuracy issues.

abstract_ko: This study investigates how the use of ChatGPT for revision in English writing classes affects the development of writing skills of ten primary pre-service teachers in the areas of content, organization, vocabulary, grammar, and mechanics of their writings, as well as their affective domains. To this end, qualitative data were analyzed from the first drafts written by participants during a process-oriented writing phase, and the final drafts revised after they received feedback from ChatGPT as well as their reflective journals. The results show that ChatGPT feedback significantly improved the content and the organization of primary pre-service teachers’ essays by encouraging them to add more details and examples, and to structure their ideas in a more logical and coherent manner. The findings also indicate that using ChatGPT as a revision tool helped them to select more appropriate vocabulary, correct grammatical errors for clarity, and use writing mechanics, such as spelling and punctuation, more accurately. Furthermore, with the support of ChatGPT, primary pre-service teachers reported increased interest in writing activities, greater confidence in sentence construction, enhanced motivation for essay writing, and more cautious and reflective attitudes towards using ChatGPT as a writing assistant.

abstract_ko: This study examines the effects of using QuillBot, an AI-based learning tool, on English vocabulary acquisition among Korean university students. It also investigates learners’ perceptions toward AI app-based English vocabulary learning in order to establish an effective vocabulary learning method and teaching plan for self-directed learning. Quantitative data from pre- and post-vocabulary tests, five vocabulary quizzes, and pre- and post-surveys of 45 students taking a Basic TOEIC class as part of the liberal arts curriculum at D University in Chungcheongnam-do were analyzed. A qualitative analysis was also conducted on open-ended survey responses and learners’ experiences and opinions recorded in learning journals. The findings are as follows. First, learners using the AI tool showed statistically significant improvements in all quantitative vocabulary tests and quizzes. Second, positive responses were recorded regarding learner awareness and the effectiveness and satisfaction of using AI tools in vocabulary learning. Third, participating students frequently mentioned vocabulary learning support, learning efficiency, and self-directed learning as advantages. As in previous studies, the disadvantages included meaning distortion, limited free features, and a lack of detailed feedback due to limitations in the functionality, usability, and accessibility of the AI tool. Based on the findings, several educational suggestions are discussed.

abstract_ko: This study examines the effectiveness of ChatGPT as a pedagogical tool in L2-English writing instruction over a semester. With L1-Korean college students as participants, the study compares the outcomes of a peer-interacted group (n = 34) with those of an AI-interacted group (n = 42). Both groups wrote argumentative essays responding to the same prompts and completed identical pre- and post-writing activities, including brainstorming and debating given essay topics. The only difference lay in the learners’ interaction partners during the activities: peers or ChatGPT. The results of a pretest and four posttests (three immediate and one delayed), scored on content, language use, and organization, show that the AI-interaction group consistently outperformed the peer-interaction group, specifically in content on the first posttest and language use on subsequent posttests. Furthermore, the peer-interaction group’s scores sharply declined on the delayed posttest, while the AI-interaction group maintained consistent performance, suggesting lasting benefits of interacting with ChatGPT. Follow-up interviews, however, revealed the learners’ ambivalence toward using ChatGPT in their writing process. The students appreciated the AI’s prompt and effective editing; however, they raised concerns about its lack of creativity and originality as well as the ethics of incorporating its content suggestions into their essays. Pedagogical implications and potential avenues for future research are discussed.

title_en: Elementary school teachers’ perceptions and training needs for English AI digital textbooks
kw_ko: AI 디지털 교과서; 기술 수용; 영어교육; 초등 교사; 제2언어교사교육

abstract_ko: 본 연구는 초등교사의 영어 AI 디지털교과서(AIDT)에 대한 인식과 연수 요구를 탐색하고자 하였다. 이를 위해 다양한 지역의 초등교사 66명을 대상으로 설문조사를 실시하였고, 교사 9명을 대상으로 서면 면담을 실시하였다. 수집된 자료는 빈도분석 및 주제분석을 중심으로 양적, 질적 분석을 활용한 혼합분석방법으로 분석하였다. 주요 연구 결과는 다음과 같다: 첫째, 실시간 발음 평가 및 피드백 제공, 학생 맞춤형 학습 경로 제공, 게임화 요소를 활용한 학습 참여 유도 등에서 AIDT가 유용한 것으로 보았다. 향후 영어 AIDT를 수업에 실제 적용 계획에 대해서도 대체적으로 긍정적이었다. AIDT가 학습자 참여를 촉진시키는데 도움이 된다고 보았다. 영어 AIDT 연수가 대체적으로 영어 교수에 유용하다고 보았다. 영어 AIDT에 대한 기대(학생들의 학습 흥미와 동기 유발, 학생 맞춤형 학습 지원, AI 기반 영어 평가 및 피드백 제공 등)와 우려(기기 및 네트워크 환경 문제, 교사의 활용 역량 부족, 학생 간 학습 격차 심화, 콘텐츠 신뢰성 부족)를 나타내었다. 둘째, 교사들은 이론 중심의 연수보다 실습 위주의 실제 기반 연수, 그리고 대면과 온라인을 병행하는 혼합형을 선호하였다. 연수 참여 여건과 접근성이 개선되기를 바라고 있었다. 다양한 형태의 연수 기회 확대, 교사학습공동체와 연계 운영, 우수 사례 시스템 구축 등의 정책 및 지원이 있기를 바랬다. 셋째, 교직 및 영어 교수 경력에 따라 인식과 요구가 유사하면서도 다른 점이 있었다. 고경력 교사들은 기술의 교육적 활용 가능성과 한계를 신중하게 고려하는 한편, 저경력 교사는 새로운 수업 도구에 대한 흥미와 수용 태도가 높았다. 교육연수에서 고경력 교사들은 자료 수정 및 보완, 학습자 맞춤형 기능의 실제적용 등에 관심이 있는 반면, 저경력 교사들은 AIDT 활용법과 구체적인 사례를 알고 싶어 하였다. 연수 경험 유무에 따라 상이하였는데, 연수 경험이 있는 교사들은 도구의 기능뿐 아니라 수업 맥락에 맞는 활용 방식을 스스로 구상하거나 이미 실천하고 있었으며, 연수 미경험자는 도구 자체에 대한 이해 부족과 적용 거리감을 나타냈다. AIDT 관련 연수 기회 및 참여 가능성, 그리고 AIDT에 관한 정보 접근성이 근무 지역 및 환경에 따라 차이가 나타나기도 하였다. 넷째, AIDT의 실제 수업 적용시 어려운 점은 교실 상황에 맞지 않는 콘텐츠, 학생 수준과의 괴리, 기기 및 네트워크 환경의 불안정성, 기능 숙지 어려움, 학습 흐름 단절 우려, 수업 시간 내 활용 분량 조절의 어려움 등으로 나타났다. 영어 AIDT의 안정적 수업 적용을 위해 초등교사들이 제시한 개선 요구는 AIDT 활용에 적합한 수업시간 확보, 실제 수업 중심의 실습형 연수 확대, 교사 간 공동수업 및 협업체제 구축, 업무 경감을 위한 행정 지원, 학교 관리자 및 동료교사의 협조 강화, 정기적인 후속 연수 및 컨설팅 등으로 나타났다. 본 연구는 초등영어 AIDT의 적용과 개선, AIDT의 적용을 위한 교사교육 및 전문성 신장에 대한 필요성과 시사점을 던져주고 있다.

title_ko: A Comparative Study on the Use of Papago and ChatGPT in English Writing by Korean University Students
title_en: A Comparative Study on the Use of Papago and ChatGPT in English Writing by Korean University Students
kw_en: Papago; ChatGPT; survey; English writing; prompt guidelines
abstract_ko: This study compares the results of English open-ended writing assignments completed by 21 university students using two machine translation tools, Papago and ChatGPT. A survey was also conducted to examine their perceived usefulness and differences. To investigate the impact of English proficiency, participants are divided into two groups based on their TOEIC scores: above 600 and below 600. The analysis reveals that in the Papago-based writing tasks, there are noticeable differences in grammar and vocabulary usage between the two groups, while the results for content, structure, and mechanics are similar. In contrast, for the ChatGPT- based writing tasks, although the below-600 group uses prompts more frequently, the quality of their writing outcomes is similar to that of the above-600 group. This suggests that the quality of ChatGPT outputs depends more on the content of the prompts than on their frequency of use, and is largely unrelated to English proficiency. Survey results show that both groups raise concerns about overreliance on ChatGPT, including ethical issues and the potential decline in critical thinking and English language skills. These findings suggest the need for clear guidelines on how to use ChatGPT effectively.

title_en: A Case Study of College EFL Students’ Reflections on ChatGPT Use for Reading and Writing: Implications for Digital Literacy
kw_en: ChatGPT; digital literacy; reflection; reading; writing; college English; case study
abstract_ko: As AI tools such as ChatGPT become more common, offering both advantages and drawbacks, it is important for learners to think critically about how they use them. Effective use of these tools requires digital literacy skills, encompassing functional, higher-order thinking, social awareness, and cooperation. This case study examined 12 college EFL students in a course where ChatGPT was extensively integrated into reading and writing tasks. Data came from student reflection logs and instructional materials collected after each ChatGPT session. Using inductive content analysis and deductive thematic analysis, the study found that students were capable of identifying benefits and limitations of ChatGPT for literacy practices. Moreover, student reflection logs revealed evidence of all digital literacy skills, along with overlapping areas and an uneven emphasis across skills. Overall, this study underscored digital literacy as both a prerequisite and an outcome of AI-integrated language learning and highlighted reflective practice as a critical component of this process.

kw_en: AI literacy; quest-based learning (QBL); English content development; ideathon; gamification
abstract_ko: This study designed and implemented an AI-powered English content ideathon grounded in the quest-based learning (QBL) framework to enhance learners’ AI literacy, creative problem-solving, and content planning skills. Conducted over four months at D University, the program comprised five sequential quests—Exploration, Challenge, Implement, Reflection, and Showcase—integrating principles of gamification to foster motivation and engagement. Eleven undergraduate participants from diverse majors engaged in phased tasks that incorporated generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Canva to conceptualize, refine, and prototype projects in English content development. Final outputs included video presentations, storyboards, and posters with embedded QR codes for exhibition. Projects ranged from tourism and cultural promotion to English education, including a university entrance exam-focused reading and grammar learning app prototype. Qualitative analysis of post-program reflections revealed that the QBL structure facilitated immersion, guided idea development, and cultivated transferable skills such as teamwork, critical thinking, and self-directed learning. Participants reported a shift in perception of AI from a simple information retrieval tool to a strategic partner in content creation. The study highlights the potential of integrating generative AI, QBL, and gamification into higher education, offering a scalable, interdisciplinary model for learner-centered AI literacy education in English content creation.

abstract_ko: This study investigated the effectiveness of a ChatGPT-integrated instructional approach in a college-level English composition course. The course employed a mixed instructional model: traditional teacher-centered instruction during the first half of the semester and ChatGPT-assisted learning in the second half. Data were collected through three stages of writing proficiency tests (pre-, mid-, and post-tests), writing self-efficacy surveys, weekly writing assignments, and student surveys and interviews. The findings revealed notable improvements in students’ writing proficiency and writing self-efficacy following the implementation of ChatGPT-based instruction. Additionally, the analysis of student writing demonstrated enhanced organization and linguistic accuracy. Students expressed positive perceptions of ChatGPT and employed it strategically for idea generation, lexical variation, and error correction. These results suggest that integrating generative AI tools such as ChatGPT can effectively support the development of writing skills and learner autonomy in EFL contexts.

abstract_ko: The study explores the effects of a professional development program on English language instructors’ (1) knowledge, (2) practical skills, and (3) self-efficacy in incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) into their pedagogical practices. Grounded in the theoretical frameworks of cognitive apprenticeship and socio-constructivism, the study was conducted with 15 university-level instructors. Data were collected from two primary sources—participants’ perspectives and recorded teaching sessions—using four tools: pre- and post-course interviews, weekly instructional implementations, reflective journals on AI use, and course feedback. The findings indicate that the training program had a substantial impact, fostering enhanced integration of AI into teaching practices. Participants demonstrated notable development in their conceptual understanding, instructional competence, and confidence in using AI tools. Furthermore, the study identified several challenges and constraints, offering insight into the multifaceted nature of preparing language educators for AI-enhanced instruction. This course may thus serve as a replicable model for fostering AI readiness among English language teachers.

Twenty-one students participated in a semester-long project creating short-form videos. Pre- and post-survey results, analyzed using paired sample t-tests, indicated modest but non-significant gains in multimodal expression and interpretation, with stable preferences for multimodal learning. Critical thinking showed significant improvement, while creative thinking increased slightly without statistical significance. Qualitative data revealed that AI tools facilitated meaningful learning experiences by supporting creative tasks and language practice. These findings offer valuable pedagogical implications and suggest future directions for integrating AI into English language education.

title_en: Integrating Generative AI and Machine Translation into EFL Reading and Vocabulary Instruction
kw_en: machine translators; AI; ChatGPT; reading comprehension; vocabulary; students’ perception
abstract_ko: This study investigated the effects of machine translators, ChatGPT, and their combined use on reading comprehension and vocabulary acquisition among 120 university students enrolled in English courses in 2024, who were randomly assigned to one of three tool-based groups. It also examined whether tool usage in EFL reading contexts led to varying outcomes and explored students’ perceptions of these tools. Results showed that all three groups improved in reading and vocabulary within groups, but no significant differences were found between groups. Additionally, learners’ perceptions regarding both the affective and motivational influence, as well as the educational impact of AI tools, showed no significant variation across experimental groups for the majority of survey items. Students who used machine translators found them helpful for understanding texts and reading speed but expressed concerns about inaccuracy, overuse, and unclear meanings. Those who used ChatGPT appreciated its usefulness and speed but also noted similar issues to those observed in the Machine Translation (MT) group. The group using both tools found them useful, clear, and fast, but still faced issues related to overreliance and occasional errors. Despite its limitations, this study provides an empirical example of integrating AI tools into foreign language education and offers meaningful pedagogical implications.

abstract_ko: This study aims to investigate the impact of an artificial intelligence tool, ChatGPT, on English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners’ speaking skills, including fluency, lexical range, grammatical range with accuracy, and content. Learners’ perceptions and attitudes toward using an AI-mediated speaking tool to enhance their English-speaking skills were also qualitatively explored. Fifty students from a university in Seoul were assigned to an experimental group, which engaged in communicative tasks using a generative AI-powered voice interaction tool, and to a control group, which practiced without the aid of the tool. Data were collected through (1) a pre- and post-test on speaking skills and (2) a post-survey on affective attitudes administered to the experimental group. A five-point Likert scale online survey assessed students' perceptions of the tool’s use. Results revealed that the post-test speaking scores of the experimental group were significantly higher than those of the control group, which interacted with peers. The group using the AI tool showed significant improvement in EFL learners’ speaking skills. Analyses of the survey responses indicated high levels of perceived usefulness and positive attitudes toward the AI tool, and the study underscores that such positive attitudes significantly influence learners’ intention to adopt ChatGPT for English-speaking practice.

abstract_ko: This paper aims to analyze the effects of AI chatbots and artificial intelligence speakers (application) on elementary school students in English vocabulary classes. Thirty students in grades 4–6 were randomly divided into two groups, A and B. Vocabulary tests (pre-post) and surveys (pre-post) on affective domains were used to collect data. The experimental classes consisted of six sessions using AI chatbots and AI speakers for group A (n=15), and Classcard application for group B (n=15). The results of the research are as follows. First, there was a statistically significant difference in vocabulary achievement between the two groups. Second, the findings of the survey suggested that there were significant differences at the overall affective domains (interest, confidence). To be specific, the experiment using AI tools for learning English vocabulary proved effective in improving young learners' vocabulary skills and enhancing interest, confidence, and immersion. In conclusion, AI chatbots-based teaching and learning methods can improve students’ English vocabulary abilities and positive attitudes toward foreign languages. This study emphasizes the potential of AI-assisted classes to suggest an effective approach to English vocabulary learning. If more systematic and diverse AI-based teaching & learning models are designed and implemented to improve English vocabulary instruction, it is expected to have pedagogical effects on the future classes. Furthermore, AI-incorporated classes need to be expanded and applied to higher education.

Paired-sample t-tests, ANOVA, and post-hoc analysis were conducted to compare learners’ performance in vocabulary and reading before and after ChatGPT-assisted classes. The findings of this study suggest that ChatGPT-assisted vocabulary and reading sessions were effective. Statistical analysis demonstrated a significant enhancement in learners’ academic outcomes. In addition, the lower-level group exhibited a higher degree of improvement in achievement than the intermediate and advanced groups. This suggests that ChatGPT-based English instruction significantly enhances the foundational comprehension among lower-level learners and supports their comprehensive language learning outcomes.

First, most learners expressed satisfaction with the explanations and answers provided by ChatGPT. Second, they were generally pleased with both the content and format of its suggestions, noting that ChatGPT offered new perspectives and helped deepen their understanding of discussions and literary works. Third, learners also recognized that some explanations were occasionally inaccurate, misaligned with the content, or contained potential errors. As shown in this study, while learners responded positively overall, they also pointed out issues—particularly errors—that impact ChatGPT’s reliability.

abstract_ko: This study investigates the integration of ChatGPT into a flipped learning–based English literature course, focusing on students’ perceptions and uses of the tool in group discussions. Drawing on survey data and reflective writings, the research identifies both pedagogical benefits and instructional challenges of ChatGPT in higher education. Reported benefits include diverse perspectives, efficiency, immediate feedback, informational support, and enhanced critical thinking. Concerns, however, center on plagiarism risks, factual inaccuracies, algorithmic bias, and reduced engagement. abstract_ko: This study applied the principles of the technology acceptance model (TAM) to the use of generative AI in EFL academic writing courses at a Korean university. Quantitative data was collected from 111 participants through the use of a questionnaire. In addition, qualitative data was gathered through the use of a limited number of short answers questions which were included as part of the participants' homework assignments. Quantitative data was analyzed through the use of both inferential and descriptive statistics, and qualitative responses were analyzed using a qualitative thematic review. Both sets of data were examined holistically to identify patterns and trends in relation to the TAM. The results indicate participants use generative AI frequently, and they feel it is both useful and easy to use with a moderately strong correlation between both constructs. However, this is often dependent on certain societal elements (peer usage; validation from instructors; trust). Furthermore, certain emotive factors (guilt; pleasure) can also be influential. Finally, the desire for generative AI to replace these types of courses in the future remains unclear despite an overall perception that this technology is going play an ever-increasing role in this educational context. Administrational and educational implications are also discussed.

abstract_ko: This study investigates various measures of grammatical diversity for automated speaking assessment (ASA) with Korean learners of English. Data were extracted from the Korean monologue set in the International Corpus of Asian Learners of English and classified into two proficiency groups. Using two NLP toolkits, i.e., the Biber tagger and the argument structure construction annotator, we measured the grammatical diversity of the speaking data based on six features over three levels (i.e., word, phrase, and clause), and conducted correlation and binomial logistic regression analyses. The results reveal significant correlations among the features, particularly between those related to part-of-speech and the others. It is also found that only the clause-level feature of the subordination type frequency significantly predicts proficiency levels. These findings provide insights into the potential of grammatical diversity as a valuable metric in ASA systems for Korean learners of English.

abstract_ko: This study aims to examine the effects of revision activities using a neural machine translation (NMT) tool on elementary students’ English writing skills, self-directed learning competence, and perceptions of using NMT in their writing. Over a 15-week period, 20 sixth-grade students at an elementary school in Seoul participated in a 39 writing sessions. The writing process consisted of three stages: pre-writing in L1, English composition, and post-writing (revising by comparing the translation output with their own writing, followed by reflection). Data were collected through pre- and post-writing assessments, a self-directed learning inventory, perception surveys, and interviews. The data were mainly analyzed quantitatively, with supplementary qualitative analysis. The findings revealed three key outcomes. First, the revision activity significantly improved overall writing fluency and content development, especially among mid- to lower-level learners, while spelling and expression accuracy also showed gradual progress. However, grammatical accuracy did not improve consistently and even declined for some high-level learners. Second, self-directed learning notably increased, particularly in areas such as planning, interest, and perceived learning value, supported by the task’s structured process and iterative feedback. Lastly, students’ perceptions of the NMT tool shifted from a passive aid to an active self-monitoring resource, fostering their critical use and strategic engagement. This study offers meaningful insights into the pedagogical use of NMT tools in elementary English writing instruction.

abstract_ko: This study explores the utility of ChatGPT, a large language model (LLM), for automated linguistic analysis in English as a Second Language (ESL) contexts. It examines whether ChatGPT can generate quantitative metrics, analyze learner prompts, assess vocabulary exposure, and evaluate questioning strategies. Ninety-nine CEFR A1 learners completed two structured chat tasks with ChatGPT. Data analysis was conducted using structured prompts and calibration procedures within ChatGPT-4o. Quantitative metrics (e.g., word counts, question types, sentence complexity) and qualitative classifications (e.g., vocabulary themes, follow-on question types) were generated by the model, formatted in .csv outputs, and partially verified through human-in-the-loop review. Results of transcript analysis indicate that ChatGPT effectively produces useful quantitative data including measures of sentence complexity and prompting skills. It also offers qualitative analysis of vocabulary exposure and investigative themes. Analysis of questioning skills revealed student ‘Wh’ word use and follow-on inquiry patterns. Despite noted strengths, ChatGPT showed limitations in analysis consistency, suggesting the need for teacher oversight. Recommendations include training educators in prompt-based analysis, guiding students in metric interpretation, and further validating LLM-generated data.

A mixedmethod approach was employed to gather data. First, to develop scale items assessing students'ChatGPT usage purposes, the experiences of Korean high school students using ChatGPT for Englishlearning were collected through simulations, reflection logs, and open-ended surveys. Second, a surveywas conducted with 171 participants using a newly developed instrument to measure their purposesfor using ChatGPT. Various statistical techniques, including exploratory factor analysis (EFA), latentprofile analysis (LPA), repeated measures ANOVA, and multivariate ANOVA, were used to analyzethe data. The key findings of the study are as follows: EFA identified four main purposes for usingChatGPT: reading comprehension, linguistic analysis and correction, writing support, and reading testpractice, with reading comprehension being the most favored. Moreover, LPA identified four learnerprofiles: Active User, Comprehension Seeker, Writing and Metaknowledge Seeker, and Passive User,which demonstrated notable differences across the identified purposes. The findings highlightsignificant variations in ChatGPT usage patterns among EFL learners, suggesting the need forpersonalized teaching strategies to enhance learner-AI interaction.

The findings of the study were as follows. First, pre-service elementary teachers, like inservice teachers, acknowledged the positive features of AIDT, such as personalized learning andreal-time feedback. title_ko: Urban and Rural Students’ Experiences with AI PengTalk in English Learning: A Comparative Case Study
title_en: Urban and Rural Students’ Experiences with AI PengTalk in English Learning: A Comparative Case Study
kw_en: AI-assisted language learning; PengTalk; urban and rural education; elementary EFL learners; gamification
abstract_ko: This comparative case study examined the experiences of urban and rural elementary school students in Korea using PengTalk, an AI-based English learning application. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study analyzed student surveys, usage records, and interviews. Quantitative data were examined through descriptive statistics and Mann-Whitney U tests, while qualitative responses were analyzed thematically. Both groups expressed positive perceptions, especially regarding PengTalk’s gamified and interactive features. Urban students outperformed their rural peers in average scores (82.5 vs. 75.8) and cumulative totals (28,224 vs. 12,369). However, gamification alone was insufficient to sustain engagement, particularly in the rural school. Major challenges included limited digital literacy and inadequate instructional support in the rural school, as well as technical issues such as voice recognition errors in the urban school. The findings indicate that student engagement with AI tools depends not only on application design but also on contextual factors such as access, support, and digital infrastructure. This study concludes with recommendations for more inclusive and equitable AI-assisted language learning environments.
